frame: You cannot really share an agent. You can share its context, a skill, its output or an interface, and the one you pick is a strategy decision.
Access is a switch somebody flips, and it completes in a minute. Absorption happens in other people's weeks, at their pace, for their reasons.
An agent is context, a boundary, a set of checks and somebody who answers for what it does. The first three copy in an afternoon. The fourth does not copy at all
Your candidate is not competing with nothing. It is competing with that.
narrative: Six months from now, the teammate went back to the incumbent.
By the decision meeting, the urgency had gone. New priorities had come up, and fires were burning elsewhere. The proposal got neither a yes nor a no.
A sharing plan that ends when the result is delivered stops where that project stopped.
You now have the teammate's job and a candidate selected against it.
pov: At the start of 2026 I set out to redesign a whole value stream with agents.
The leadership had not done the analysis. People they trusted had. Companies, even when they go agentic, work first and foremost on the human principle.
Your memory has been working for you for days now. It catches things you'd have missed, keeps a tone you taught it
The question arrives on its own: *could this help someone else?*
stance: *"Share the whole agent"* is a vendor pitch and is NOT on the list.
the product being sold as a shared agent is always three of the four parts, with the fourth still sitting with whoever built it.
A polished technical file beside a people file full of unnamed roles is the finding, not a finished rollout.
Accountability is the part with a name on it, and a name does not travel inside a folder.
